conditions_echo: Declared by the teacher and used as given: unsupervised; individual; AI permitted; anything at home, the internet and an AI assistant permitted as resources; summative purpose; time not stated; sent home over a week at the end of the industrialization unit; students have done sourcing practice on other documents but these two excerpts are new to them.
reviewer_notes: Novelty holds for every item on this page: the teacher states both excerpts are new to the students, and the item set is claim-targeted, with each of H1 through H4 addressed by a named item and the scoring line mapping onto H4 requirement by requirement. Two of the three conditions are therefore met throughout, and the instrument's coverage of the four claims is complete at component level, which is why Gate 1 fails for all four claims rather than for want of analysis. The condition that fails is independence, and it fails uniformly: supervision is declared 'unsupervised' and an AI assistant is expressly permitted, so no item on the page produces an independent observation and every claim's booleans come out the same way. Under the feed-forward rule the entire packet leaves the room with the student for a week, so nothing in it - including the sourcing lines and the two-paragraph argument - is secured by being written down. All five items are constructed response, so no guess-rate caveat applies anywhere in this assessment. Author and year for both documents are printed in the document headers, which is worth the teacher knowing when reading item 1 even setting the conditions aside. This is a diagnosis of what the declared conditions license, not a comment on the assessment's design or on the teacher's practice.
